sourceNote: The new Tripo P2 rabbit mesh with its quads (assets/models/rabbit/README.md). The hand rig assets/models/rabbit/tripo-hand/rabbit.blend starts from it in headless Blender with the calls of tools/blender/studio_armature.py (design 4.4, "Hand rig").
name: Rabbit

studio.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py): the pelvis turns back until the hip angle opens by open degrees, as seated string players sit tall. The shares fall from the spine1 to the head in equal steps, so that the head stays level. The value 0 keeps the trunk of the source.
studio.bindArmsNote: With straightArms, bindArms.upper_arm sets the bind upper arm, and bindArms.forearm sets only the elbow axis: the cross product of the bind upper arm and this forearm direction (StudioBody.hinges, bind_hinges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The two directions are the directions of the old bent bind of the fox of main, so that the elbow axes and the zero of the roll of the upper arm stay. The paw has no bind direction, because it keeps the turn of the upper arm.
studio.straightArmsNote: The bind keeps the arms of the source straight: the forearm and the paw keep the turn of the upper arm, so that the rest shape holds the bend of no role, and each hold bends the elbow and the wrist from the same shape (the role-neutral bind of design 4.4).
studio.bindSupinationNote: The bind paws take no supination (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so the bind forearms have no twist. On the Tripo rabbit, a bind supination twisted the bind forearm, and the crease angle then showed the diagonals of its quads (assets/models/rabbit/README.md, "Arm twist").
studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 15 degrees down and 8 degrees out, and the shin leans 12 degrees forward of vertical, so that most of the thigh lies on the seat (uv run --no-project --with numpy python -I tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 15 8 12).

tone.note: No move: the cream fur of the texture is near the cream of the sheet in the light of the app.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at a grid of samples. A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples are below dark. A dark face in the eye box is an eye, and a face in the nose box near the nose color is the nose. A palette of palette colors (k-means in Oklab) keeps the colors few.
colors.eyeBoxNote: The eye box holds the two loose eyeballs of the source (|x| 0.018 to 0.066, y 0.672 to 0.73, z 0.052 to 0.098 in the source). The nose box holds the pink nose tip.

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most points points of their edge, lifted along the normal of the eye. pnpm studio-body drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The faces of the old eye take the main color of the ring around it.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail (seat_masks() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The front edge lies seatGap units behind the knee joint of the bind (the property seat of the armature), so that the calf does not reach over the seat.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, as on the other bodies. Bone heat gives them their weights.

jointsNote: The places are the places of the source, mapped by the paw turns of the hand rig (assets/models/rabbit/README.md). The hand rig makes no point edit. The source places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The FBX has no armature, so each joint comes from sections of the mesh and its edge loops. Arm (closed rings of 10 vertices): the shoulder joint at x 0.07, the elbow at x 0.1475, the wrist at x 0.225, the knuckles at x 0.268, and the tip at x 0.31. Leg (closed rings of 12 vertices): the hip joint at (0.0595, 0.287, 0.004) in the haunch, the knee at y 0.178, the ankle at y 0.055, the ball of the foot at z 0.055, and the toe tips at z 0.095. Trunk: the hips at y 0.31, the neck at y 0.585, and the head from y 0.615 to 0.80. Ears: the root at y 0.785, the tips at (0.10, 1.0, -0.065). Tail: a short bone from (0, 0.33, -0.08) back. The hip joint lies 0.5 mm forward of the measured place (z 0.0035), because with z 0.0035 the rest frames of the leg bones in Blender scale by 3e-5 (the thigh points nearly opposite to its parent), above the limit of pnpm rig-export.
bodyNote: The facts of the body (BODY_FACTS of tools/studio-body.ts) beside the height: the crease angle 180, so that each corner takes the mean normal of the faces at its vertex, as the smooth shading of an FBX viewer shows the source, and a seat 1 cm deeper, so that the back keeps off the chair back.
eyeSizeNote: The head height H of the body in units, as studio-body measures it on the export, before the head size. The hand rig keeps the eyes of the mesh, so it places no pea eye.
metersPerUnitNote: The scale of the app: H (0.2018 units of the source form) is 0.2985 m, the H of the rabbit of main. The hand rig keeps the form of the source, so only the scale of the whole body sets H. The fact height of the armature is the shoulder joints at this scale.
chairNote: The seat of the rig in units of this body, as the property seat of the armature of tripo-hand/rabbit.blend holds it.
rollSplitNote: Each vertex keeps its total weight on the 4 roll segments of an upper arm or a forearm, and the total goes to the two segments around its place along the bone by a linear ramp (roll_split() of tools/blender/simple_rig.py). Bone heat gave the segments their weights by distance, so the roll gathered in bands at the segment borders: the roll share changed up to 4.1 times the even rate, and the faces there showed a spiral of long facets.
